name: account-change
description: A user or group was created, or a user was added to a privileged group (sudo, wheel, admin, root, docker, lxd). Wazuh rule group `adduser`: 5901 new group, 5902 new user, 5904 user changed, 100211 / 100212 usermod / gpasswd into a privileged group (T1098). Possible persistence. Triage procedure: nodes/cases/thehive/docs/TRIAGE.md.

tasks.title: Identify the change
tasks.description: From the alert: new account or group, who created it, host, time.

tasks.title: Is there a change request?
tasks.description: Check with the host owner whether the change was planned. Planned: false positive, note the reference.

tasks.title: Check the new account's activity
tasks.description: Logins, sudo use and files owned by the new account since its creation (Grafana / Wazuh).

tasks.title: Contain if needed
tasks.description: Unplanned: request the account disable through the n8n playbook (approval) and set containment-action to user-disabled; treat the host as possibly compromised.

tasks.title: Document and close
tasks.description: Write the summary, set the resolution status and close.

name: ids-network-alert
description: Network intrusion detection alert from the Suricata sensor (D49), read by a Wazuh agent from Suricata's EVE JSON: built-in rule 86601 "Suricata: Alert - <signature>", rule groups `suricata` / `ids`. Suricata severity 1 → Wazuh level 12, 2 → 10 (Wazuh W3.5). Triage procedure: nodes/cases/thehive/docs/TRIAGE.md.

tasks.title: Review the signature
tasks.description: Read `data.alert.signature`, its category and `data.alert.severity`, the source and destination (`data.src_ip`, `data.dest_ip`, `data.dest_port`) and the protocol. Is this traffic expected for this host?

tasks.title: Check IP reputation
tasks.description: n8n has already run the automatic analyzers at intake; re-run the Cortex analyzers (MISP) on the source and destination IP observables if needed. Note whether the external side is known malicious.

tasks.title: Check the internal host
tasks.description: Look for other Wazuh alerts on the internal host around the same time (Grafana, or the "seen before in Wazuh?" analyzer once C13 exists): new processes, logins, file changes.

tasks.title: Decide and respond
tasks.description: True positive: request the IP block through the n8n playbook (with approval) and set containment-action to ip-blocked. False positive: note the signature and the reason for Suricata / Wazuh tuning.

tasks.title: Document and close
tasks.description: Write the summary (what, impact, action taken), set the resolution status and close the case.

name: ioc-match
description: A Wazuh event matched an IOC exported from MISP into a CDB list (Wazuh rule group `misp_ioc`, range 108xxx; contract C14): IP, domain or hash listed in MISP. Check whether it comes from the SOC's own events or a public feed before marking it IOC. Triage procedure: nodes/cases/thehive/docs/TRIAGE.md.

tasks.title: Identify the indicator
tasks.description: Which value matched (IP, domain, hash), which host and event. Open the MISP event behind it (the MISP analyzer on the observable shows it).

tasks.title: Confirm the hit
tasks.description: Is the indicator still valid (MISP event date, tags, warninglists)? An old or common value can be a false positive.

tasks.title: Scope: other hosts
tasks.description: Search Wazuh for the same value on other agents (Grafana, or the "seen before in Wazuh?" analyzer once C13 exists).

tasks.title: Contain
tasks.description: Request the IP block through the n8n playbook (approval) and set containment-action; for a hash, follow the malware-detection tasks.

tasks.title: Document and close
tasks.description: Write the summary, keep the confirmed indicator marked as IOC, set the resolution status and close.

name: malware-detection
description: Malicious or suspicious file detected on a host (Wazuh syscheck / rootcheck, VirusTotal or YARA integration, known-bad hash). Triage procedure: nodes/cases/thehive/docs/TRIAGE.md.

tasks.title: Identify the file
tasks.description: From the alert: file path, SHA-256 hash, agent (host), user, and which Wazuh module detected it. Add the hash and file name as observables if missing.

tasks.title: Analyze the hash
tasks.description: Run the Cortex analyzers (MISP; VirusTotal once enabled) on the hash. Record the verdict and malware family in the case summary.

tasks.title: Scope: other hosts
tasks.description: Search Wazuh (Grafana / scripts/wazuh-query.sh) for the same hash or file name on other agents. Add every affected host as a hostname observable.

tasks.title: Contain the host
tasks.description: If confirmed malicious: request host isolation through the n8n playbook (analyst approval) and set containment-action to host-isolated.

tasks.title: Eradicate
tasks.description: Remove the file and its persistence (with the host owner), verify with a new Wazuh scan, then request the host to be released from isolation.

tasks.title: Share IOCs and close
tasks.description: Mark confirmed hashes / domains / IPs as IOC so they can go to MISP (with the Cortex + MISP owner). Write the summary, set the resolution status and close.

name: network-scan
description: Many blocked ports or connections from one source seen by the pfSense firewall (Wazuh rule groups `pfsense` + `recon`, range 103xxx, T1046). Usually reconnaissance. The alert arrives over syslog: the host is the firewall (`predecoder.hostname`), not a Wazuh agent. Triage procedure: nodes/cases/thehive/docs/TRIAGE.md.

tasks.title: Identify the source
tasks.description: From the alert: source IP, targeted hosts and ports, time window, internal or external source.

tasks.title: Check reputation
tasks.description: Cortex analyzers (MISP) on the source IP. Known scanners (warninglists) are usually noise.

tasks.title: Any follow-up?
tasks.description: Did any connection from that source get through (allowed traffic, Suricata alerts, logins)?

tasks.title: Respond
tasks.description: Internal source: treat the host as possibly compromised. External and persistent: request the IP block through the n8n playbook (approval) and set containment-action to ip-blocked.

tasks.title: Document and close
tasks.description: Write the summary, set the resolution status and close.

name: privilege-escalation
description: sudo failures or other attempts to gain root privileges (Wazuh W2.2, rule group `sudo`). Triage procedure: nodes/cases/thehive/docs/TRIAGE.md.

tasks.title: Identify the user and command
tasks.description: From the alert: user, command attempted, host, number of failures.

tasks.title: Expected or not?
tasks.description: Is this user supposed to use sudo on this host? A typo by an admin is a false positive; an unknown user or command is not.

tasks.title: Look for follow-up activity
tasks.description: Search for a later successful sudo / root session, new users or changes to /etc (Grafana / Wazuh).

tasks.title: Contain if needed
tasks.description: If malicious: request the account disable through the n8n playbook (approval) and set containment-action to user-disabled.

tasks.title: Document and close
tasks.description: Write the summary, set the resolution status and close.

name: ssh-bruteforce
description: Many failed SSH logins against a host (Wazuh sshd rules such as 5710, 5712, 5716, 5720, 5763). Main risk: a later successful login from the same source. Triage procedure: nodes/cases/thehive/docs/TRIAGE.md.

tasks.title: Confirm the attack
tasks.description: From the alert: source IP, targeted user name(s), number of failed attempts and time window. Is the source internal or external?

tasks.title: Check for a successful login
tasks.description: Search Wazuh for a successful SSH login (rule 5715) from the same source IP after the attack. If there is one: raise the severity to Critical and treat the host as compromised.

tasks.title: Check the source IP
tasks.description: Run the Cortex analyzers (MISP) on the source IP observable. Record the result in the case summary.

tasks.title: Check the targeted accounts
tasks.description: Do the targeted accounts exist? Are they privileged (root, admin)? Recommend disabling root / password SSH login on the host if allowed.

tasks.title: Block the source IP
tasks.description: Request the IP block through the n8n playbook pb-ssh-bruteforce (analyst approval; active response arrives with C9 in Phase 2) and set containment-action to ip-blocked.

tasks.title: Document and close
tasks.description: Write the summary (source, accounts, outcome, action taken), set the resolution status and close the case.

name: suspicious-login
description: A successful login that shouldn't happen: a login after repeated failures from the same source (built-in rule 40112, level 12) or an SSH login as root (100200, level 10). Possible account compromise. Triage procedure: nodes/cases/thehive/docs/TRIAGE.md.

tasks.title: Confirm the sequence
tasks.description: From the alert: source IP, account, number of failures, time of the success, service (SSH, console, web).

tasks.title: Was it the real user?
tasks.description: Check with the account owner or known locations / schedules. If not confirmed: raise the severity to Critical.

tasks.title: Review the session
tasks.description: Look for what the account did after logging in (sudo, new users, file changes, outbound connections) in Grafana / Wazuh.

tasks.title: Contain the account
tasks.description: If compromised: request the account disable through the n8n playbook (approval) and set containment-action to user-disabled; block the source IP if external.

tasks.title: Document and close
tasks.description: Write the summary, set the resolution status and close; ask for a password reset.

name: wazuh-generic
description: Default template for any Wazuh alert without a specific template. Triage procedure: nodes/cases/thehive/docs/TRIAGE.md.

tasks.title: Review the alert
tasks.description: Read the rule description, level, agent and full log in the alert. Look in Grafana (SOC Overview, filtered on the agent) for related alerts around the same time.

tasks.title: True or false positive?
tasks.description: False positive: set the resolution status to False positive and write the reason, so the Wazuh owner can tune the rule. True positive: continue.

tasks.title: Analyze the observables
tasks.description: Run the Cortex analyzers (MISP) on every IP, domain, URL and hash observable. Add any new observable you find.

tasks.title: Contain if needed
tasks.description: If the host or account is at risk: request the containment through the matching n8n playbook (analyst approval) and set containment-action. Never change systems by hand.

tasks.title: Document and close
tasks.description: Write the summary (what happened, impact, action taken), set the resolution status and close the case.
